title: How to raise a seed round in 2026: investor funnel, qualifying VCs, moats vs AI labs
summary: Jason Calacanis answers community questions on fundraising mechanics, how startup costs collapsed, and differentiating from frontier AI labs. Treat fundraising as a full-time sales funnel, judge investors by behavior rather than words, and build community, multiplayer and human services around what LLMs won't ship.

principles.text: Judge investors by what they actually invest in, not what they say in meetings.
principles.quote: You have to divorce what people say in social settings especially investors from their behavior.

principles.text: Seed fundraising is a numbers game: about 150 targets, 50 meetings, 15 second meetings, two term sheets.
principles.quote: you need to contact 150 seed funds, get 50 meetings with seed funds to get 202 meetings to get two to give you a term sheet.

principles.text: Run fundraising as a qualified sales funnel and make it a full-time job for one co-founder.
principles.quote: You have to look at fundraising as a full-time job. You have to collect investors and build deep, meaningful relationships with them over time.

principles.text: If too early for later-stage investors, use accelerators for a first check and customers, then return.
principles.quote: get your 125k, your 25k check, your 250k check, get your first five customers and then you can go back to them and they might be a greater later stage.

principles.text: Differentiate from AI labs with features, community, multiplayer and human services the model interface won't add.
principles.quote: there's always going to be a feature set that the interface of the large language model is not going to add because of clutter and confusion.

principles.text: Hardware is now a moat and investors have reversed their stance; fund it via investors or Kickstarter pre-sales.
principles.quote: hardware is is the only one of the only moes left.
